title: New Business Rule: How Many Whole Life Insurance Policies One Owner May Hold
content:
**Rule.** An owner may hold any number of Ashgrove Whole Life Insurance policies on lives in which the owner has an insurable interest; there is no maximum number of policies per owner. The total face amount on one insured life is governed by the aggregate face limit per insured. An Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life policy may not be issued on an insured who already has Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life coverage in force.

## Condition and result

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| An owner applies for a further whole life policy on a life in which the owner has an insurable interest | The number of policies the owner already holds is no bar; the count is not capped |
| The application is for an Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life policy and the insured already has Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life coverage in force | The policy may not be issued |
| The face amount applied for on one insured | Measured against the aggregate face limit per insured life |

## Basis questions

**Does an owner who already holds four Whole Life Insurance policies reach a ceiling on the number of policies?** No. The count of policies per owner is not capped; the face amount on each insured life is what is limited.

**May a second Final Expense policy be issued on the same insured while the first is in force?** No. A Final Expense policy may not be issued on an insured who already has Final Expense coverage in force.
